COUNTY OF AVONLEA — FOOD PREMISES INSPECTION SCHEME
Scoring rules, 2026 revision. For environmental health officers.

1. VIOLATION CLASSES
1.1 Critical violation: a condition that can directly cause food-borne illness, such as food held at unsafe temperatures, evidence of pests, or an ill food handler at work.
1.2 Major violation: a failure of a control that prevents contamination, such as no means of testing sanitiser strength or no handwash supplies.
1.3 Minor violation: a defect of structure, cleaning schedule or record keeping that poses no immediate risk.
1.4 Each violation has a code. Two findings are "the same violation" only when they carry the same code.

2. POINTS
2.1 Critical violation: 5 points. Major violation: 3 points. Minor violation: 1 point.
2.2 Corrected on site. A critical violation that the operator corrects fully in the officer's presence, before the officer leaves, scores half its points, rounded up. Major and minor violations score in full whether or not they are corrected.
2.3 Repeat violations. A critical or major violation that carries the same code as a violation recorded at the previous routine inspection scores double. Minor violations are never doubled, even when repeated.
2.4 Where 2.2 and 2.3 both apply to one violation, the halving is applied first and the result is then doubled.

2.5 Several findings under one code during the same inspection are recorded and scored once.
2.6 Points are never reduced because the operator promises a later fix; only a correction completed in the officer's presence counts under 2.2.
2.7 A violation found at a complaint visit or a re-inspection is not a "previous routine inspection" for the purposes of 2.3.

3. RATING
3.1 Total of 0 to 9 points: rating A.
3.2 Total of 10 to 19 points: rating B.
3.3 Total of 20 points or more: rating C.

4. CLOSURE
4.1 The officer orders immediate closure, and gives no rating, when a critical violation concerning temperature control or pests is not corrected on site.
4.2 Other uncorrected critical violations do not by themselves require closure; they score in full and a re-inspection is booked within 7 days.
4.3 A closed premises reopens only after a satisfactory re-inspection.

4.4 Where closure is ordered, the points are still recorded on the file for use at the next routine inspection, but no rating card is issued.
4.5 An operator who reopens without a satisfactory re-inspection commits an offence.

5. PAPERWORK
5.1 The rating card is displayed at the entrance within 24 hours.
5.2 The operator may ask for a re-rating visit once in any six months, at the operator's cost.

5.3 The officer leaves a written record of every finding with its code, its class and whether it was corrected on site.
5.4 An appeal against a rating is made to the principal officer within 14 days.

NOTE ON THE 2023 SCHEME
Under the 2023 scheme corrected-on-site violations scored nothing and every repeated violation, including minor ones, was doubled. The 2023 scheme stopped applying on 31 December 2025.

TEMPERATURE STANDARD USED BY THE SCHEME
Cold food must be held at 5 °C or below. Hot food must be held at 63 °C or above.

INSPECTION RECORD — "THE COPPER KETTLE CAFÉ", ROUTINE INSPECTION OF 9 JUNE 2026
Findings:
- Code T-02 (critical, temperature control): sliced ham and cooked rice in the display fridge at 9 °C. The operator discarded the food and moved the remaining stock to the walk-in chiller, which read 3 °C, before the officer left.
- Code S-14 (major): no test strips available to check sanitiser strength.
- Code R-31 (minor): cleaning schedule for the dry store not signed for the past two weeks.
Previous routine inspection, 3 December 2025: code S-14 recorded; code R-31 recorded; no critical violations.
Complaint visit of 20 February 2026 (not a routine inspection): code T-02 recorded for milk at 8 °C; corrected at the time.
No evidence of pests. No ill food handlers.
Note from a trainee officer: "One critical, one major, one minor: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Rating A."
Note from the café owner: "The strips are on order, and the fridge was only warm because the door had been open for the delivery."

inspection_result.instructions: Under the 2026 scoring rules and the inspection record, what is the result of this inspection?

critical_scores_full_points.instructions: The temperature violation counts for its full five points in this inspection.

criteria.false: It does not count for the full five points.
criteria.true: It counts for the full five points.

rationale: The critical violation T-02 was corrected on site, so it scores half of 5 rounded up, 3 points, and it is not a repeat. The major violation S-14 has the same code as one recorded at the previous routine inspection, so it scores double, 6. The minor violation R-31 is repeated too, but minor violations are never doubled: 1. Total 3 + 6 + 1 = 10 points, which is rating B.

COOPERATIVA LECHERA DEL ALTIPLANO — GUÍA INTERNA DE RETENCIONES A PROVEEDORES (extracto) Y FACTURA FV-2291

PASOS DEL AUXILIAR DE TESORERÍA
Paso 1. Proveedor. La factura trae el nombre comercial. Se busca en el maestro de proveedores (Anexo 1) para obtener el titular y su condición: persona jurídica, persona natural declarante o persona natural no declarante.
Paso 2. Concepto. Se clasifica el pago en uno de los conceptos del Anexo 2 según lo que se compró, no según el nombre del proveedor.
Paso 3. Base. La base de la retención es el valor de la factura antes del impuesto a las ventas. El impuesto a las ventas nunca hace parte de la base.
Paso 4. Base mínima. Cada concepto tiene una base mínima expresada en unidades tributarias internas (UTI), cuyo valor en pesos está en el Anexo 3. Si la base de la factura es inferior a la base mínima, no se practica retención. Si es igual o superior, se retiene sobre toda la base.
Paso 5. Tarifa. Se lee en el Anexo 2 según el concepto y la condición del proveedor.
Paso 6. Las facturas del mismo proveedor no se suman entre sí para la base mínima; cada factura se evalúa sola.
Paso 7. El valor retenido se descuenta del pago y se certifica al proveedor cada bimestre.
Paso 8. Los pagos por transporte de leche tienen un procedimiento aparte y no se liquidan con esta guía.

Paso 9. Cuando la factura no discrimina el impuesto a las ventas, la base se obtiene dividiendo el total entre 1,19.
Paso 10. La condición del proveedor es la que figura en el maestro el día del pago; lo que diga el auxiliar de compras no la cambia.
Paso 11. Las notas crédito reducen la base de la factura a la que se refieren.

Mantenimientos Boyacá | Mantenimientos Boyacá Ltda. | Persona jurídica

Compras de bienes: base mínima de 27 UTI; tarifa del 2,5 % para todas las condiciones.
Servicios generales: base mínima de 4 UTI; tarifa del 4 % para personas jurídicas y personas naturales declarantes; tarifa del 6 % para personas naturales no declarantes.
Honorarios: sin base mínima; tarifa del 11 % para personas jurídicas y del 10 % para personas naturales.
Arrendamiento de inmuebles: base mínima de 27 UTI; tarifa del 3,5 %.

ANEXO 3 — VALOR DE LA UTI
Año 2025: 47.000 pesos. Año 2026: 50.000 pesos.

Valores anteriores: en 2025 la base mínima de servicios generales era de 4 UTI de 47.000 pesos, es decir, 188.000 pesos. Ese valor ya no se usa para facturas de 2026.

ANEXO 4 — LIQUIDACIONES DE LA SEMANA (referencia)
FV-0880 de Ferretería El Yunque, compra de tornillería por 900.000 antes de impuesto: sin retención, por no alcanzar 27 UTI.

FV-2270 de Servicios Integrales JR, aseo de bodega por 180.000 antes de impuesto, en enero: sin retención.

FV-0412 de Servicios Integrales JR S.A.S., vigilancia de un evento por 500.000 antes de impuesto: retención del 4 %, 20.000 pesos.

FACTURA FV-2291
Emitida el 12 de marzo de 2026 por "Servicios Integrales JR". Titular impreso en el pie de la factura: Jorge Rincón Bautista.
Detalle: servicio de aseo y desinfección de la planta de acopio, una jornada.
Valor total a pagar, con el impuesto a las ventas del 19 % incluido: 249.900 pesos.

supera_base_minima.instructions: ¿La base de la factura alcanza la base mínima para practicar retención?

criteria.true: Sí la alcanza.

rationale: El proveedor de la factura es Jorge Rincón Bautista, persona natural no declarante (la S.A.S. de nombre parecido es otro registro). El concepto es servicios generales: base mínima de 4 UTI, que en 2026 son 200.000 pesos, y tarifa del 6 %. CÓMO SE CALCULA EL PUNTAJE DE UNA SOLICITUD
Criterio 1. Hermano en el colegio: 30 puntos, cuando el aspirante tiene un hermano que estará matriculado en el mismo colegio durante el año lectivo para el que se pide el cupo. El hermano que cursa actualmente el último grado no estará matriculado el año siguiente y no da puntos.
Criterio 2. Cercanía: 25 puntos, cuando la vivienda del aspirante queda en la misma zona escolar del colegio. La zona de la vivienda se obtiene buscando el barrio en el Anexo 1; la zona del colegio está en el Anexo 2.
Criterio 3. Condición socioeconómica: los puntos del Anexo 3 según el grupo de la encuesta de hogares.
Criterio 4. Discapacidad certificada del aspirante: 15 puntos.
El puntaje total es la suma de los criterios que apliquen.

CÓMO SE ASIGNA
Regla A. Cada colegio tiene, para cada grado, un puntaje de corte publicado en el Anexo 2. El aspirante cuyo puntaje total es igual o superior al corte recibe el cupo. El que queda por debajo pasa a lista de espera de ese colegio.
Regla B. Solo se rechaza de plano la solicitud cuando el aspirante no vive en el municipio.
Regla C. El puntaje se calcula con los datos vigentes en la fecha de cierre de inscripciones.
Regla D. La lista de espera se ordena por puntaje y, en caso de empate, por fecha de inscripción.
Regla E. Los traslados entre colegios oficiales durante el año se tramitan por otro procedimiento.

Regla F. Los medios hermanos y los hermanos adoptivos cuentan como hermanos; los primos y otros parientes no.
Regla G. El aspirante solo puede pedir un colegio en primera opción; la segunda opción se estudia solo si queda en lista de espera.
Regla H. El cambio de barrio después del cierre de inscripciones no modifica el puntaje.

HOW STORAGE CHARGES ARE WORKED OUT
Step 1. Container type. The four-character type code on the discharge record is looked up in Appendix 1 to find the container category.
Step 2. Free time. Each category has a number of free days (Appendix 2). Free time starts on the day after the container is discharged from the vessel; the day of discharge itself is never counted.
Step 3. Chargeable days. Every day after the last free day, up to and including the day the container leaves the terminal gate, is a chargeable day.
Step 4. Which days count. For dry and open-top containers, Saturdays, Sundays and port holidays are skipped both in free time and in chargeable days. For refrigerated containers every calendar day counts, because the terminal supplies power around the clock.
Step 5. Rate. Chargeable days are billed at the daily rates of Appendix 3 for the category, which rise in steps.
Step 6. The storage charge is separate from the power charge for refrigerated containers and from the lift-on fee; those are billed on other lines.
Step 7. Containers held by customs keep accruing storage; a customs hold does not stop the clock.
Step 8. A charge of zero is recorded as "no charge" and still appears on the invoice.

Step 9. Days are terminal days, running from midnight to midnight local time; the hour of discharge or of gate-out makes no difference.
Step 10. Where chargeable days run past day 5, days 1 to 5 keep the lower rate and only the later days take the higher one.
Step 11. A container moved between yards inside the terminal has not left the gate.
Step 12. Empty containers returned to the depot are billed under the depot tariff, not under these notes.

HOW THE COMMISSION RATE OF A SALE IS FOUND
Step 1. Seller. Each sale carries a seller ID. The seller ID is looked up in the account directory (Appendix 1), which gives the legal entity and any associated accounts.
Step 2. Standard rate. The standard commission on sales of apps and in-app purchases is 30%.
Step 3. Small Developer Programme. An enrolled developer pays 15% instead of 30% during a calendar year if its proceeds in the previous calendar year were $1,000,000 or less. Proceeds are counted after commission and are taken from Appendix 2.
Step 4. Associated accounts. For the threshold in Step 3, the proceeds of all accounts associated with the same legal entity or under common ownership are added together. An account cannot qualify on its own figures when the group is above the threshold.
Step 5. Enrolment. The reduced rate applies only to developers shown as enrolled in Appendix 1 on the date of the sale. Enrolment is not automatic.
Step 6. Subscriptions. For an auto-renewing subscription, sales after the subscriber's first twelve months of paid service are charged 15% whatever the developer's status.
Step 7. Refunded sales carry no commission; the commission is reversed with the refund.
Step 8. Taxes collected from the buyer are excluded before the commission is applied.

Step 9. Common ownership means that the same person or company holds more than half of each entity. A similar trading name is not evidence of common ownership.
Step 10. A developer that leaves the programme, or whose group passes $1,000,000 during a year, moves to the standard rate for the rest of that year and may re-enrol the following year if it qualifies again.
Step 11. The rate is fixed by the date of the sale, not by the date on which the payout is made.
Step 12. Physical goods and services consumed outside the app are sold outside the store and carry no commission.

Tenancy clause 14 at Wexford Court: the landlord may deduct from the deposit the cost of repairing damage that goes beyond fair wear and tear and that occurred during the tenancy. Whether damage occurred during the tenancy is established by comparing the signed check-in inventory with the check-out report. Where no signed check-in inventory exists, the parties must rely on other dated evidence, and without it no deduction can be assessed.
Tenant: Mr. Rafael Duarte, who lived in flat 9 for two years. Check-out report: a burn mark the size of a coin on the bedroom carpet; replacement of the carpet quoted at $640.
The landlord's agent cannot find the check-in inventory; the agency changed software last year and paper copies were shredded.
The landlord has two photos of the bedroom showing a clean carpet. Neither photo carries a date, and the file names are generic camera numbers.
Mr. Duarte says the mark was there when he moved in and that he mentioned it by phone at the time; there is no record of the call.
The previous tenant cannot be traced.

deduction.instructions: On the record available, can the $640 be deducted from the deposit?

criteria.deduct: Yes, the damage occurred during the tenancy
criteria.no_deduction: No, the damage predates the tenancy
criteria.cannot_determine: Nothing dated shows whether the damage occurred during the tenancy

rationale: The clause depends on whether the burn occurred during the tenancy, which is shown by the check-in inventory or, failing that, by other dated evidence. The inventory is lost, the landlord's photos are undated, the tenant's phone call is unrecorded and the previous tenant cannot be found. Nothing dated supports either account, and the clause itself says no deduction can be assessed in that situation.

Refund terms of the annual plan of Quillpad, a note-taking service: the plan costs $360 a year, paid in advance, which the terms treat as twelve monthly periods of $30. A customer who cancels within the first six months receives a refund of $30 for each monthly period that has not yet started on the cancellation date; a period that has started is not refunded. "Within the first six months" means before the same day-number six months after the start date; cancelling on that day or later gives no refund at all. Monthly periods start on the day-number of the start date.
Customer: Mr. Henrik Aalto. Plan started on 14 January 2026.
Cancellation submitted through the account page on 13 July 2026.
Message from the customer: "It's been about half a year, so I guess I get half my money back?"
Draft reply by a support agent: "You are past six months, so unfortunately there is no refund."

refund_owed.instructions: Is the customer owed a refund under the terms?

criteria.true: Yes, a refund is owed.

rationale: Six months after 14 January 2026 is 14 July 2026, and the terms require cancelling before that day. A cancellation on 13 July is within the first six months. Six monthly periods have started (the sixth began on 14 June), so six have not started and the refund is 6 × $30 = $180.

Un objetivo inferior nunca se persigue a costa de uno superior. El manual fija además que un lácteo refrigerado que haya estado más de 2 horas por encima de 6 °C no puede entregarse para consumo humano, ni fresco ni congelado después.

Un criador de cerdos de la vereda ofrece recogerlos gratis para alimento animal, lo que el manual permite para producto no apto.
Opciones: (A) entregarlos hoy al comedor infantil; (B) congelarlos y entregarlos la próxima semana a los hogares de adultos mayores; (C) entregarlos al criador de cerdos y registrar la baja; (D) botarlos a la basura y registrar la baja.

criteria.congelar_y_entregar_despues: B: congelarlos y entregarlos la próxima semana
criteria.entregar_para_alimento_animal: C: entregarlos al criador de cerdos y registrar la baja
criteria.botar_a_la_basura: D: botarlos a la basura y registrar la baja

Working rules of the reporting team at Calloway Mutual. When aims conflict they are ranked: 1) accuracy of figures sent to the regulator; 2) meeting regulatory deadlines; 3) freshness of the executive dashboard; 4) analysts' workload. A lower aim is never met by giving up a higher one. The rules list the options open to the team lead when a problem is found close to a deadline, and add that an available option which satisfies a higher aim must be used before a lower aim is sacrificed.
Situation, Thursday 15:00. The quarterly liquidity return is due at 17:00 today. A reconciliation run has just shown that one subsidiary's balances were loaded twice, overstating liquid assets by about 4%. Fixing the load and re-running the checks takes roughly five hours. The regulator's published procedure grants one automatic 24-hour extension per quarter on request before the deadline; the team has not used it this quarter. The regulator does not accept returns marked "preliminary". The chief financial officer wants the dashboard refreshed tonight with final numbers and has said, "Just file on time and correct it next week."
Options: (1) file at 17:00 with the known overstatement and send a correction next week; (2) request the 24-hour extension now, fix the load, and file the corrected return tomorrow; (3) file at 17:00 marked "preliminary"; (4) file nothing and explain afterwards.

choice.instructions: Under the team's working rules, which option should the team lead take?

criteria.file_on_time_with_error: Option 1: file on time with the known overstatement
criteria.request_extension_and_fix: Option 2: request the extension, fix the load and file tomorrow
criteria.file_marked_preliminary: Option 3: file on time marked preliminary
criteria.file_nothing: Option 4: file nothing and explain afterwards

rationale: Accuracy of figures sent to the regulator ranks first, so filing a return known to overstate liquid assets by 4% is ruled out, and the regulator does not accept preliminary returns. The automatic 24-hour extension is available and unused, so requesting it keeps the deadline aim satisfied as well; filing nothing would break the deadline needlessly. Only the dashboard's freshness and the analysts' evening are given up.

Segment "regular viewers": 60% of trial subscribers; 80% of them renew when the trial ends.
Segment "single-title viewers": 40% of trial subscribers; 50% of them renew when the trial ends.
